messages.content:
The following text was generated by one of these five AI language models:
GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek.

All five options are AI-generated - do not consider the possibility that a human wrote it. Read the text carefully and identify which model most likely produced it, based on writing style, structure, and phrasing.

Reply with JSON only, in exactly this form and nothing else:

{"model": "<one of GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek>", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "<one short sentence>"}

confidence: 1 = pure guess, 5 = certain.

--- TEXT ---
Volunteering your time to help others is often described as an act of generosity, but it is also an investment in your own growth. When you volunteer, you place yourself in situations that may require communication, organization, problem-solving, leadership, teaching, fundraising, or teamwork. These are practical skills that can strengthen your confidence and make you more capable in professional settings. Volunteering also connects you with people you might never meet otherwise, including community leaders, nonprofit staff, business owners, educators, and other motivated volunteers. Those relationships can expand your professional network in a natural and meaningful way, sometimes leading to mentorship, references, job opportunities, or collaborations.

Volunteering also gives you a stronger sense of purpose and meaning. Daily life can sometimes feel repetitive or overly focused on personal responsibilities, but helping others reminds you that your actions matter beyond your own immediate concerns. Whether you are serving meals, tutoring a student, visiting older adults, cleaning up a public space, or helping at a local event, you can see the direct effect of your effort. That sense of contribution can make life feel more grounded and valuable because you know you are part of something larger than yourself. Even small acts of service can create a powerful feeling that your time has been used well.

Finally, volunteering can improve mental health by reducing feelings of isolation. Many people struggle with loneliness, especially when work, school, family duties, or life changes limit social connection. Volunteering creates a reason to show up, interact with others, and build relationships around shared goals. It can replace passive loneliness with active participation and give people a supportive community where they feel seen and useful. Helping others can also shift attention away from personal worries and create moments of gratitude, connection, and emotional relief. In this way, volunteering benefits both the people receiving help and the person giving it, making it one of the rare choices that strengthens a community while also strengthening the individual.
--- END ---
Output the JSON object described above, and nothing else.
